items.title: European stocks rise as oil eases after sharpest weekly surge since 2022

featured_image.name: European stocks to open higher amid easing oil price, Iran war

items.description: Global financial markets entered Friday on uncertain footing as the escalating conflict between the United States and Israel on one side and Iran on the other continued to roil energy markets and rattle investor confidence. European stocks opened higher on Friday as oil prices eased slightly from their sharpest weekly surge since 2022, according to CNBC, though Asian equities largely fell amid persistent concerns over supply disruptions and inflation.[1]

items.title: Asian markets mixed as Iran conflict enters 7th day

featured_image.name: Asian shares are mixed in cautious trading after a mixed day on Wall Street

items.description: Financial markets capped a turbulent week on Friday as Asian shares traded mixed and oil prices edged lower, offering a brief reprieve from the volatile swings that have rattled investors since the United States and Israel launched joint military strikes on Iran on February 28. The conflict, now in its seventh day, has closed the Strait of Hormuz, disrupted global energy supplies, and sent shockwaves through every major asset class.

items.title: Israel launches 'broad-scale' strikes on Tehran, Beirut

featured_image.name: Tehran says Israeli fighter jets used US-controlled airspace over Iraq to attack  Iran as death

items.description:
Israel unleashed what it called a "broad-scale wave of strikes" on Tehran and carried out 26 airstrikes on southern Beirut early Friday as the war across the Middle East entered its seventh day, with U.S. officials warning that the bombardment was about to intensify further.

The Israel Defense Forces said overnight that it had begun targeting "Iranian terror regime infrastructure in Tehran," posting about the operation on Telegram just after 4 a.m. local time. Observers on the ground described the strikes as the heaviest yet on the Iranian capital, with explosions shaking residential neighborhoods, the area around Tehran University, and a military academy. Al Jazeera's correspondent in Tehran reported "a relentless series of massive strikes" accompanied by fighter jets and thick smoke.[1][2][3]

items.title: Oil retreats as US weighs futures market action

featured_image.name: Markets News, March 5, 2026: U.S. Indexes Tumble as Oil Hits $80 a Barrel; Dow Closes Down Almost 800 Points

items.description:
Markets around the world lurched through another volatile session on Thursday as the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran entered its seventh day, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average briefly plunging more than 1,000 points before oil prices pulled back from their highs on reports of possible US government intervention in futures markets.

The Dow shed 784 points, or 1.6%, closing at 47,954.74, according to The Wall Street Journal, after US crude surged past $80 a barrel for the first time since summer 2024. The S&P 500 fell 0.6% and the Nasdaq Composite lost 0.3%, reversing a Wednesday rally that had been fueled by reports Iran was open to indirect negotiations with Washington.[1][2][3]

items.title: Physicists create first computer model of 'ideal glass'

featured_image.name: Scientists open new window on the physics of glass formation

items.description: A team of physicists at the University of Oregon has created the first computer model of an "ideal glass," a long-theorized material in which molecules are packed as tightly and stably as possible while maintaining the disordered, amorphous structure that defines glass. The achievement, published in Physical Review Letters, addresses a challenge first posed nearly eight decades ago and could eventually reshape how advanced materials are designed and manufactured.[1][2]

items.title: Cambridge scientists discover 'molecular catapult' in solar materials

featured_image.name: Molecular 'catapult' fires electrons at the limits of physics

items.description: Scientists at the University of Cambridge have observed electrons crossing the boundary between solar materials in just 18 femtoseconds — less than 20 quadrillionths of a second — propelled by molecular vibrations acting as a "catapult." The discovery, published March 5 in Nature Communications, challenges decades of assumptions about how charge moves through solar energy systems and could reshape the design of more efficient light-harvesting technologies.[1][2]

items.title: UN report finds migratory species decline accelerating

featured_image.name: Migratory fish species are in drastic decline, a new UN report details

items.description:
The plight of the world's migratory species has worsened over the past two years, with 49 percent of populations protected under a United Nations treaty now declining and 24 percent facing extinction, according to an interim report released this week by the Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species of Wild Animals (CMS). The findings represent a sharp deterioration from the landmark 2024 assessment, which found 44 percent of species declining and 22 percent threatened with extinction.[1][2][3]

The report, developed by the UN Environment Programme World Conservation Monitoring Centre (UNEP-WCMC) and other contributors, will be presented at CMS COP15, set to convene in Campo Grande, Brazil, from March 23 to 29.[2][3]

items.title: Jimmy Lai won't appeal 20-year Hong Kong sentence

featured_image.name: Hong Kong's Jimmy Lai Decides Against Appealing 20-Year ...

items.description:
Jimmy Lai, the 78-year-old founder of Hong Kong's now-defunct Apple Daily newspaper, has decided not to challenge his conviction or 20-year prison sentence under Beijing's national security law, his legal team confirmed on Friday, bringing an end to one of the most closely watched cases in the city's history.

"We confirm we have clear and definitive instructions not to lodge an appeal against conviction or sentence," Lai's lawyers told The Associated Press and Reuters, without providing further explanation for the decision.[1][2]

items.title: Amazon fixes 6-hour shopping outage after turbulent week

featured_image.name: Amazon data centers struck, damaged by drone strikes in ...

items.description: Amazon resolved an hours-long outage on Thursday that left tens of thousands of shoppers unable to complete purchases, view prices, or access their accounts — capping a turbulent week in which Iranian drone strikes had already knocked three of the company's Middle East data centers offline.

items.title: SoftBank seeks record $40B loan to fund OpenAI bet

featured_image.name: OpenAI closes $40 billion funding round, largest private tech deal on record

items.description:
SoftBank Group is seeking a loan of up to $40 billion to help finance its latest investment in OpenAI, according to Bloomberg, in what would be the Japanese conglomerate's largest-ever borrowing denominated solely in dollars.[1][2]

The 12-month bridge loan will be underwritten by four lenders, including JPMorgan Chase, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg. Talks with banks are ongoing and details could change, the people said. Spokespeople for both JPMorgan and SoftBank declined to comment.[1]

items.title: US weighs oil futures intervention, grants India Russian crude waiver

featured_image.name: Treasury Secretary Bessent says U.S. will make 'series of announcements' to support oil trade in the Gulf

items.description: The Trump administration moved on multiple fronts Thursday to contain surging energy prices driven by the war with Iran, granting India a 30-day waiver to purchase sanctioned Russian crude and signaling it may take the unprecedented step of intervening in oil futures markets.

items.title: EU split deepens over rolling back climate rules to cut energy costs

featured_image.name: European Union proposes world's strictest emissions rules ...

items.description: European governments are retreating from key climate commitments as the economic fallout from the loss of cheap Russian energy collides with mounting industrial pressure to lower power prices. With EU leaders set to tackle electricity costs at a summit on March 19, a deepening rift has emerged between member states over how far to roll back the bloc's climate architecture.

items.title: US reports 90 percent drop in Iranian ballistic missile attacks

featured_image.name: Number of Iranian ballistic missiles fired plunges since start of Operation  Epic Fury

items.description: Iranian ballistic missile attacks have plummeted by 90 percent since the start of Operation Epic Fury, U.S. Central Command chief Adm. Brad Cooper announced Thursday during a press briefing at CENTCOM headquarters in Tampa, Florida. Drone attacks have fallen by 83 percent over the same period, Cooper said, as U.S. and Israeli forces continue to degrade Tehran's offensive military capabilities in what has become the largest American buildup in the Middle East in a generation.[1][2]

items.title: Trump urges Iranian diplomats worldwide to seek asylum

featured_image.name: Donald Trump bets big on the Iran war

items.description:
President Donald Trump called on Iranian diplomats around the world to request asylum and help shape "a new and better Iran" during a White House event on Thursday, as the US and Israel pressed ahead with a military campaign now in its sixth day.

"We also urge Iranian diplomats around the world to request asylum and to help us shape a new and better Iran with great potential," Trump said at a ceremony honoring Inter Miami's 2025 MLS Cup championship, before pivoting to an extended briefing on the conflict.[1][2]

items.title: Iran warns EU will 'pay the price' for silence on war

featured_image.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran- Iran Foreign  Ministry Spokesman rejects EU officials claims as baseless

items.description: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei warned European Union countries on Thursday that they will "pay the price, sooner or later" if they remain silent on the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran, which Tehran considers a violation of international law. The remarks, made during an interview with Spanish public broadcaster TVE, came as the conflict entered its sixth day with no sign of de-escalation.[1][2][3]

items.title: UAE weighs freezing billions in Iranian assets

featured_image.name: Exclusive | U.A.E. Explores Freezing Iranian Assets to ...

items.description:
The United Arab Emirates is considering freezing billions of dollars in Iranian assets held within the Gulf state, a move that could sever a key economic lifeline for Tehran as the conflict between the U.S., Israel, and Iran enters its second week, according to The Wall Street Journal.[1]

The potential asset freeze comes as Iran continues to pummel the UAE with missiles and drones in retaliation for the U.S.-Israeli strikes that killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei late last month. As of March 4, the UAE defense ministry reported intercepting 175 of 189 ballistic missiles and 876 of 941 drones launched against the country since February 28, with the attacks killing three foreign nationals and injuring 78 others.[2][3]

items.title: Trump says Iran seeking deal as US strikes continue

featured_image.name: Trump says Iran is 'running out of launchers' as regime is 'being ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump declared on Thursday that Iran is calling the United States to negotiate a deal, even as US and Israeli military operations against the country showed no signs of slowing. Speaking at a White House event celebrating Inter Miami CF's MLS Cup championship, Trump pivoted to the war in Iran, claiming the Iranian regime was seeking an end to hostilities but that Washington was in no rush to stop fighting.

"They're calling, they're saying, 'How do we make a deal?' I said, 'You're being a little bit late,'" Trump said, according to remarks reported by the Jerusalem Post and the Straits Times. "And we want to fight now more than they do."[1][2]

items.title: Ukraine, Russia swap 200 POWs each as peace talks stall over Iran war

featured_image.name: Russia and Ukraine start biggest prisoner swap of the war

items.description: U.S.-brokered peace talks between Ukraine and Russia, originally planned for this week, have been postponed indefinitely as the escalating conflict in the Middle East pulls international focus away from ending the four-year war in Eastern Europe. Despite the diplomatic setback, the two sides carried out a major prisoner exchange on Thursday, returning hundreds of soldiers to their families.

items.title: Russia and Ukraine begin swapping 500 POWs each over two days

featured_image.name: Russia, Ukraine to exchange 500 prisoners of war on March 5 ...

items.description:
Russia and Ukraine exchanged 200 prisoners of war on each side on Thursday and plan to swap another 300 each on Friday, the Russian Foreign Ministry said, in what amounts to the largest single exchange between the two countries in months.[1]

Vladimir Medinsky, Russia's lead negotiator and an aide to President Vladimir Putin, announced the exchange on his Telegram channel, saying it was "part of the agreements reached in Geneva," referring to the latest round of trilateral peace talks between Russia, Ukraine, and the United States. Russia's Defense Ministry said the United Arab Emirates and the U.S. helped mediate Thursday's swap of the first 200 on each side.[2][3]

items.title: Over 330,000 displaced across Middle East, UNHCR says

featured_image.name: Israeli bombardment of Lebanon sends 100,000 fleeing to war-torn Syria: UN

items.description:
More than 330,000 people have been forcibly displaced across the Middle East and beyond as intensifying hostilities between the United States, Israel, and Iran send shockwaves through a region already hosting millions of refugees, the UN refugee agency said Thursday.[1][2]

UNHCR reported that an estimated 100,000 people fled Tehran in the first 48 hours after US-Israeli strikes began on February 28, with road police recording between 1,000 and 2,000 vehicles departing the capital daily, heading primarily toward northern provinces. Despite the internal exodus, the agency noted "no major increase in cross-border movements from Iran linked to recent events".[3][2][1]
